size.note: Newman's Birds gives 24 cm, marked M.

habitat: Singly in broad-leaved woodland, mixed bushveld, riverine forest and other well-wooded habitats, including exotic trees.
summary: A fairly common to uncommon summer visitor. The male is yellow except for black wings, black tail feathers and black lores, with a pink bill. The black mask is less extensive than a male African Golden Oriole’s. Newman says the female resembles the immature illustration and does not describe either in words. The seldom-heard call is a ringing weela-weeoo, plus a churring alarm note. Newman names no months. The Kemp paper name European Golden Oriole and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Male African Golden Oriole has a black line through the eye and black primaries, not wholly black wings.

calls.description: A seldom-heard ringing weela-weeoo, plus a churring alarm note common to all orioles. Grade A call from Parc eòlic de Rubió, Spain. No openly licensed southern African grade A call outranked it. The filename is XC244231-ORIORI15h01m19s19may2015 (2).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common to uncommon summer visitor and names no months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. The female and immature are not described in words, which is why this needs review. Population figures, the Kemp paper name European Golden Oriole and the code NB were left unchanged.
